newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN EAGER TO SHAKE OFF TITLE RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN EAGER TO SHAKE OFF TITLE RIVALS.

text.p: German league leaders Bayern Munich, overshadowed by victories for Schalke and Borussia Dortmund in Europe this week, take centre stage again on Sunday against third-placed Bayer Leverkusen.
Bayern, who went out in the first round of the UEFA Cup to Spain's Valencia, want to widen the gap at the top and shake off Leverkusen, who trail them by just five points after 20 games.

But second-placed champions Dortmund can take the top spot - at least for a day - by beating bottom side Freiburg on Saturday. Dortmund trail Bayern by three points but have the better goal difference.
Leverkusen coach Christoph Daum admitted Sunday's home game against Bayern would be an enormous challenge.
"What they have achieved is simply a sensation," Daum said. "Bayern have a lot more options than us. They will exploit any slip in concentration."
The Bavarians easily stretched their unbeaten run to 12 games last Saturday with their biggest home win of the season, thrashing unglamorous Duisburg 5-2.

But Bayern could be without Italy-bound Christian Ziege, who struck twice against Duisberg. Ziege underwent a groin operation on Thursday and will probably not be able to train for two days. Midfielder Mehmet Scholl is also doubtful because of injury.
One the plus side, however, goalkeeper Oliver Kahn could be back in action following a bout of chickenpox.
Last week Leverkusen lost ground in the title race when they managed only a goalless draw at lowly Fortuna Duesseldorf.
Daum said his team had already reached their goal of being among the top clubs who should qualify for next season's UEFA Cup.
"The most important thing for us is reaching (European) competition. Qualification for the Champions' League, for example, would be the sensation of all sensations," he said.
"We posses all the right qualities. The question is: can we activate them all consistently and at the same time?"

Dortmund, fresh from their 3-1 victory in the first leg of their European Cup quarter-final against Auxerre on Wednesday, should be boosted by the return of internationals Juergen Kohler and Heiko Herrlich for their game away to Freiburg.
But they will still be without Matthias Sammer, Brazilian Julio Cesar and Austrian Wolfgang Feiersinger, who was substituted in the Auxerre game with a groin injury.
Seventh-placed Schalke, who won the first-leg of their UEFA Cup quarter-final against Valencia 2-0 on Tuesday, are likely to be unchanged for their trip to neighbours Bochum on Friday.
